name: MonarchImpersonationBanner
title: ImpersonationBanner
wrapsNative: ViewThatFits with HStack and VStack, Text with an AttributedString, TimelineView(.everyMinute) with Date.RelativeFormatStyle, MonarchButton; placed with .safeAreaInset(edge: .top)
summary: A persistent, inverse-coloured bar shown while acting as another person, with who, since when, why, and one way out: Stop.
whenToUse: While a support or admin person is signed in as, or viewing as, another person, and anything they do happens in that person's account.
whenNotToUse: For a read-only preview with no real actions, a MonarchCalloutBanner is enough. For ordinary notices such as a trial ending, use MonarchCalloutBanner with the page placement.
api: init(name: String, detail: String? = nil, reason: String? = nil, startedAt: Date? = nil, isStopping: Bool? = nil, labels: MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels = MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels(), onStop: @escaping @MainActor () async throws -> Void)

struct MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels { init(viewingAs: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, started: String? = nil, reason: String? = nil, stop: String? = nil, stopLabel: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, stopError: String? = nil) }

options.name: name
options.description: The person being viewed as, in bold in the main line.

options.name: detail
options.description: A second identifier, such as their email, in brackets after the name in the muted inverse colour.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why the session started, such as a ticket number, after "Reason:".

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the session started, shown as "Started 5 minutes ago" and refreshed every minute.

options.name: isStopping
options.description: Controls the busy state of Stop when the app tracks the stop itself; tracked from onStop when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the main line, "Started", "Reason:", "Stop", its spoken name and the fallback error.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Ends the session. The button is busy while it runs and ignores taps; throwing shows the error's description (or the fallback) in the banner.

states.name: active
states.description: The eye icon, the main line, the start and reason line, and Stop.

states.name: stopping
states.description: Stop shows its spinner and ignores taps.

states.name: error
states.description: The failure under the text with an icon, announced; the banner stays.

appearance: Inverse colours (the inverse background with inverse text, muted inverse text for the detail and meta line) and a three-point edge and icon in the solid warning colour, so it looks unlike every other banner in light, dark and high-contrast themes. Stop is a small secondary button; when the text and button do not fit on one line, the button moves below and fills the width.
platformNotes: The web's sticky prop is replaced by placement: on iOS the app puts the banner in safeAreaInset(edge: .top) of its root view, which keeps it above scrolling content. The web's now and locale props are not needed; the relative time uses the system clock and locale. A replacement main line from labels is shown without bold, because the bold name needs the built-in format. Android builds the same component. The parity map names MonarchBanner and lists callout-banner as a dependency; the banner is drawn on its own instead, because its inverse colours, warning edge and missing dismiss button are what set it apart from callout banners, as on the web.
accessibility: The icon is decorative; the text is one element read as the main line with the name and detail, then the start and reason line.
The main line is posted as an announcement when the banner appears, like the web's status region.
Stop is named "Stop viewing as" and the name, which starts with its visible title, and has a 44-point touch target; it shows a busy state while stopping.
A failed stop is announced and shown with an icon and text.
There is no dismiss button: the only way out is to stop.
edgeCases: Long names, details and reasons wrap.
The app removes the banner when the session ends; a successful onStop does not hide it by itself.
With isStopping set, taps while it is true are ignored even if onStop has returned.
